title.value: AfriQA: Cross-lingual Open-Retrieval Question Answering for African Languages
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: AfriQA: Cross-lingual Open-Retrieval Question Answering for African Languages

extractions.description: The paper introduces AfriQA, a cross-lingual question answering dataset focused on African languages, and evaluates baseline models for this task.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on improving language technology for African languages, but does not explicitly focus on sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this work, we lay the foundation for research on QA systems for one of the most linguistically diverse regions by creating A FRI QA, the first QA dataset for 10 African languages. A FRI QA focuses on open-retrieval QA where information-seeking questions2 are paired with retrieved documents in which annotators identify an answer if one is available (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019).

primary_category.justification: The work directly addresses the deficit of African languages in existing datasets and aims to improve access to information for speakers of African languages.
primary_category.quote: This dataset directly addresses the deficit of African languages in existing datasets. We conduct an analysis of the linguistic properties of the 10 languages, which is crucial to take into account when formulating questions in these languages.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper contributes to improving access to and utilization of data in the Global South by focusing on African languages and QA systems.
primary_sub_category.quote: By building a dataset from the ground up that is specifically tailored to African languages and their corresponding cultures, we are able to ensure better contextual relevance and usefulness of this dataset.

new_primary_category.justification: There is no need for a new category.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no need for a new sub category.
